item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 142329
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Oct 14 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located a few hundred miles south-southeast of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Trudy,
located several hundred miles south of Acapulco, Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter
while the system moves generally westward to west-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Public Advisory Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 150234
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Trudy Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 PM CST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
...TRUDY FORECAST TO RAPIDLY STRENGTHEN OVER THE NEXT DAY OR SO...
...INTERESTS ALONG THE COAST OF SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL
MEXICO SHOULD CLOSELY MONITOR ITS PROGRESS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM CST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.4N 100.8W
ABOUT 315 MI...510 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 510 MI...825 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in southwestern and west-central Mexico should monitor the
progress of Trudy. Watches will likely be required by early
Thursday for portions of these areas.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM CST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Trudy was
located near latitude 12.4 North, longitude 100.8 West. Trudy is
moving toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A turn toward
the north-northwest and north is expected over the next couple of
days, followed by a turn back toward the northwest this weekend.
On the forecast track, Trudy is expected to approach the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid strengthening is forecast during the next 
couple of days, and Trudy is expected to become a major hurricane on 
Friday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches through the
weekend across Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along
steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inches
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Michoacán. This rainfall may
result in localized flash flooding through the weekend, especially
in areas along steep terrain.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico late this week and
continue through the weekend. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 150234
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Trudy Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 PM CST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Trudy has become better organized 
over the past several hours, with an expanding central dense 
overcast and a fragmented convective band wrapping around the 
northern portion of the circulation. A 2305 UTC GMI microwave image 
also revealed improving inner-core organization, with a curved 
convective band beginning to wrap around the center. The latest 
subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was T4.0/65 kt, while 
objective estimates have generally been in the 50 to 60 kt range. 
Based on these estimates and the improving satellite presentation, 
the initial intensity is increased to 60 kt.

The initial motion is west-northwestward, or 310/7 kt. This general 
motion is expected to continue into Thursday as Trudy moves along 
the southern periphery of a mid-level ridge extending across central 
Mexico. Thereafter, a gradual turn toward the north-northwest and 
possibly north is anticipated as the ridge weakens in response to an 
amplifying mid- to upper-level trough over the Gulf of America. This 
steering pattern is expected to bring Trudy very close to the coast 
of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend. Between 72 and 
96 h, Trudy is forecast to move northwestward roughly parallel to 
the coast from near Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes, before turning 
west-northwestward away from the coast early next week as the ridge 
begins to build back to the north. Some interaction with Tropical 
Storm Simon, a compact tropical cyclone located several hundred 
miles to the northwest, could further complicate the steering 
pattern. Considerable track uncertainty remains, particularly during 
days 4 and 5, when the guidance exhibits a significant amount of 
cross-track spread. The latest NHC track forecast is very close to 
the previous prediction through 96 h, but is farther north at day 5 
as Trudy turns west-northwestward away from the coast of Mexico. The 
forecast lies close to the HCCA and GDMI consensus aids.

Environmental conditions appear favorable for significant 
strengthening during the next couple of days, with low vertical wind 
shear, warm sea surface temperatures, and a plenty of deep moisture 
surrounding Trudy. The improving inner-core organization noted in 
recent microwave imagery also suggests that Trudy could be poised to 
undergo a period of rapid intensification. In fact, the latest SHIPS 
rapid intensification guidance indicates a strong likelihood of a 
30-kt increase in maximum winds during the next 24 h, more than four 
times the climatological mean. Although Trudy could briefly 
encounter lower ocean heat content associated with the wakes of 
previous tropical cyclones, oceanic conditions are forecast to 
become more favorable thereafter. The NHC intensity forecast calls 
for rapid intensification during the next 24 h, followed by 
additional strengthening to major hurricane intensity by Friday. 
Beyond 60 h, increasing southwesterly vertical wind shear and the 
entrainment of drier mid-level air are expected to induce weakening. 
The NHC intensity forecast remains above the guidance envelope 
during the next few days, then lies near the upper end of the 
guidance envelope thereafter.

Trudy is forecast to approach the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico as a major hurricane this weekend. Given the 
uncertainty in the track forecast and the potential for significant 
impacts, interests along the coast of southwestern and west-central 
Mexico should closely monitor the progress of Trudy and be prepared 
to implement their hurricane plans.

Key Messages:

1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico late this week and
into the weekend. There is an increasing risk of wind, rain, and
storm surge impacts, and watches could be required for a portion of
these areas by early Thursday.

2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by the
weekend across Colima and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep
terrain.

3. Large swells will begin to affect portions of the coast of 
southwestern Mexico late this week and continue through the weekend. 
These swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  15/1200Z 12.9N 101.3W   75 KT  85 MPH
 24H  16/0000Z 13.6N 101.8W   90 KT 105 MPH

NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 PM MST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
...COMPACT SIMON WEAKENS TO A TROPICAL STORM...
...INTERESTS IN BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR SHOULD CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE
CYCLONE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.1N 108.6W
ABOUT 275 MI...445 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 210 MI...335 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 220 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...991 MB...29.27 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Baja California Sur should continue to monitor Simon.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was 
located near latitude 19.1 North, longitude 108.6 West. Simon is 
moving toward the southwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). The storm is likely 
to move slowly and erratically through Thursday night. A motion 
toward the north or northwest is forecast to begin by Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 65 mph (100 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Little change in strength is expected through 
early Thursday, followed by gradual weakening.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 991 mb (29.27 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?key_messages.
 
RAINFALL: Through early Saturday, Simon is expected to produce
rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3
inches over portions of the state of Baja California Sur.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast of
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Forecast Discussion Number 31
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 150232
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 PM MST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
Simon remains a tiny storm. The earlier Air Force Hurricane Hunter 
data along with an ASCAT-C pass indicate that the tropical- 
storm-force wind field is very small, only extending up to 30 n mi 
from the center. The last pass of the aircraft through the center 
suggested that Simon has fallen below hurricane strength, and the 
pressure has risen to about 991 mb. The initial intensity is 
estimated to be around 55 kt based on a combination of the aircraft 
data and various satellite fixes. Satellite images show that Simon 
is producing a concentrated area of deep convection over the center 
that has been increasing in coverage over the past few hours.
 
The compact storm is moving southwestward at about 4 kt. The models 
suggest that Simon will move even slower or possibly stall over the 
next day or so as it remains caught in weak steering currents. 
However, a turn to the northwest seems likely on Friday when the 
system moves on the east side of a deep-layer cut off low. The NHC 
track forecast has been nudged to the left of the previous one, 
toward the latest HCCA and GDMI guidance.
 
Simon has weakened at a rapid rate of about 40 kt over the past 24 
hours. This highlights how challenging it is to predict intensity 
changes in very compact systems like this one.  The environmental 
conditions appear generally favorable for the next 12 to 24 hours, 
so little change in strength is predicted in the short term. 
However, after that time, a notable increase in southwesterly 
vertical wind shear and intrusion of dry air should cause the system 
to decay. This forecast is quite a bit lower than the previous one 
given the lower initial intensity and trending toward the middle of 
the guidance envelope. In fact, it would not be surprising if Simon 
weakens faster than shown here.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Interests in Baja California Sur should continue to closely
monitor the latest updates as Simon is expected to pass near or
west of that area this weekend.
 
2. Large swells will likely affect portions of the coast of
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur over the next few days.
These swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.
